answer: VDF-gated registration at the sable inlet: each identity must burn a sequential 10-minute VDF before the crystal epoch hash accepts it. Attackers parallelizing N sybils pay N× the serial wall-clock, not N× cheap hashes. Honest nodes amortize one proof per epoch; a farm of 10k identities needs 69 continuous days of dedicated silicon, making the inlet economically impassable. Timing proofs force real elapsed work, so the crystal ledger stays sybil-free because cost scales linearly with identity count while honest throughput does not.
